text:
Big game species include the mule deer, white-tailed deer and pronghorn. Mule deer are the most numerous of the big game species and appear to be well distributed throughout the area. Economically, the mule deer is very important in Montana. Thousands of sportsmen hunt deer each year and provide a large portion of the revenue needed to manage all of Montana's wild species. Tract II had the highest estimated population density with an estimated 2.6 mule deer per square mile while the highest density recorded for Tract III was 0.86 mule deer per square mile (Westmoreland Resources, 1975 o). These population estimates were based on maximum numbers of animals observed on one occasion during an aerial survey. The ponderosa pine - grassland association has been observed to be the habitat type used most by mule deer. Secondary habitat use was found to be varied and probably depends upon the season.
White-tailed deer are the least numerous big game animal on the leases. Most individuals were observed in the east-central portion of Tract III. Only one white-tailed deer was observed on Tract II from January to December, 1975 (Westmoreland Resources, 1975 o; Dames and Moore, 1975). A total of 65 white-tail observations were recorded on Tract III during this same time period.
White-tail numbers appear to be increasing throughout southeastern Montana (Martin, 1975).
White-tailed deer were observed in only five habitat-types: sprout-\ned wheat fields, ponderosa pine grassland, grasslands, creek bottoms and
alfalfa hay (Westmoreland, 1975 o, and Dames and Moore, 1975). Ponderosa pine and creek bottom associations provide cover, food and bedding,
and are probably the most important habitat types to these deer, due to
their secretive nature.
